phrases.text: Every evening, before I lock up, I tell my phone how the day went.

Today I sold two thousand four hundred: nine hundred cash, twelve hundred MoMo, and Kojo still owes three hundred. I bought seven hundred of stock with cash, paid eighty delivery, moved five hundred from bank to MoMo, Abena paid two hundred of what she owed into MoMo, and I took a hundred and fifty cash home.
Busy with a customer? I type it as it happens.
CashNarra turns my words into records.
It asks what I left out. Which account paid for delivery?
I check all eight, and I save.
Abena's two hundred is not a new sale. She owes four hundred now.
Two thousand three hundred came in. Nine hundred and thirty went out.
And the new equipment? Twenty percent there.
My day. My words. My numbers.
Tell your money story. See the numbers.
